s1
You got care. Then came the envelopes.
s2
A hospital bill. A doctor bill. A lab bill. And a letter that says: this is not a bill.
s3
We spend about five trillion dollars a year on health care, and over two hundred fifty billion is lost to administrative complexity.
s4
The same scan costs several times more across town. One in five in-network marketplace claims is denied. A hundred million people carry medical debt.
s5
Trust in doctors and hospitals fell from seventy-two to forty percent in under four years.
s6
This complexity isn't an accident. It's a design. So let's redesign it.
s7
One: know the price. Enforce the transparency laws we already have, and turn raw price files into one guaranteed, all-in price before care.
s8
Two: one bill. Plain language, settled in real time, like swiping a card.
s9
Three: no surprises. Automate prior authorization, screen everyone for financial aid before collections, and never charge more than the quote.
A price you can see. A bill you can read. A system you can trust.
